claims.text: Eutectic high-entropy alloys have dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Introducing a controlled density of nanoscale precipitates within lamellar colonies can simultaneously enhance strength and room-temperature tensile ductility.
Nanoscale precipitates act as obstacles to dislocation movement.
Obstruction of dislocation movement by nanoscale precipitates enhances strength.
Nanoscale precipitates may reduce stress concentrations at internal lamellar-colony boundaries.
Reducing stress concentrations at internal lamellar-colony boundaries improves tensile ductility.
Precipitate-modified material will have greater strength than the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
Precipitate-modified material will have greater room-temperature tensile ductility than the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The effectiveness of nanoscale precipitates depends on their size, distribution, and interactions with the matrix phases.
Specific ranges of precipitate size, distribution, and matrix interaction will provide an optimum strength-ductility balance.
The exact mechanisms and optimal precipitate characteristics are not well understood.
